summary: Neumann worked in Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Heidelberg, Munich, Göttingen under Heeren, San Lazzaro degli Armeni, and with Abel-Rémusat. He served at Gymnasium am Kaiserdom, the University of Munich (1833–1852), and the Bavarian State Library (~1833–1863).
Heider studied at Williams College (~1953–1954), Harvard College (~1954–1956), and Harvard University (~1957–1966).
An Indologist, Zistl studied at the University of Munich under Ernst Kuhn (~1908–1915). He worked as a wissenschaftlicher Hilfsarbeiter at Munich University Library from 1911 to 1952.
Active in linguistics and Indology, Rhenius studied at the Berlin Mission Seminary in 1810. He subsequently served as a missionary with the Church Mission Society from around 1814 to 1835.

Graul worked in Indology and religious studies, having studied theology at the University of Leipzig in 1834. He served as director of the Leipzig Evangelical Lutheran Mission (1844–1860) and taught Missionswissenschaft at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg in 1861.

An Indologist and philosopher, Potter studied at the University of California and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held professorships at the University of Minnesota and the University of Washington, and edited the Encyclopedia of Indian Philosophies (~1970–2019).

Hoffmann specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. After completing a PhD at Munich under Walther Wüst, Hanns Oertel, and Ferdinand Sommer, he held posts at Munich, Saarland University (1952–1955), and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (1955–1983).

Hummel, active in Indology, earned a PhD at Munich under Wilhelm Geiger (~1921–1926) and studied at Tübingen under Enno Littmann (~1930–1933). He held posts at the University of Tübingen (1935, 1946–1976) and visited the University of Tehran (1975–1976).

Jahn worked in Iranian/Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He completed a PhD at Charles University under Moriz Winternitz and also studied at Leipzig. His posts included the German University in Prague, Utrecht University (1950–1972), and Leiden University (1953–1973).
Jaspers was a philosopher who studied at Heidelberg University from roughly 1902 to 1908. He later held an academic post at Heidelberg University from around 1909 until 1948.

Jettmar worked in history/archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology. After earning his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Heine-Geldern and Bleichsteiner, he worked at the Museum of Ethnology, Vienna, and held professorships at Vienna, Mainz, and Heidelberg (1964–1986).

Active in philosophy and Indology, Windischmann studied at Mainz (Dr.med.) and Würzburg. He served as professor at Lyceum and Gymnasium Aschaffenburg (1803), court librarian at Hofbibliothek Aschaffenburg (1811), and professor at the University of Bonn from 1818.

Lachmann, a specialist in linguistics, completed studies at the University of Leipzig (~1809–1812) and the University of Göttingen (~1812–1815). He held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1825 to 1851.

Marx was a philosopher who studied at Gymnasium Friedrich Wilhelm, Bonn (under Welcker), Humboldt University of Berlin, and Jena. He held editorial posts at the Rheinische Zeitung (~1842–1843) and Neue Rheinische Zeitung (~1848–1849).

Müllenhoff worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Meldorfer Gelehrtenschule, Kiel University, Leipzig, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He subsequently held posts at Kiel University (1842) and Frederick William University Berlin (1858).

Müller worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Breslau and Humboldt University of Berlin under August Boeckh, Friedrich Schleiermacher, and Friedrich August Wolf. He held posts at Magdalenaeum Wrocław and served as professor at Göttingen from 1819.

Popper was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vienna and Cambridge. He held positions at the University of Canterbury (1937–1945), London School of Economics (1946), King's College London, and the University of London (1949–1969).

Reinhardt, a philosopher, studied at the University of Bonn and under Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held academic posts at Bonn, Hamburg, Goethe University Frankfurt (~1923–1951), and the University of Leipzig (~1942–1945).

Lepsius worked in history/archaeology and linguistics, studying at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Berlin under August Boeckh. He held positions at the German Archaeological Institute at Rome, Humboldt University of Berlin, the Egyptian Museum, and directed the Prussian State Library (1873).

Rosenkranz was a philosopher who studied at Berlin under Hegel, Heidelberg, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held an Extraordinariat at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1831) before succeeding Herbart with a chair and rectorate at the University of Königsberg in 1833.
